rocky-patel--vintage-1990.description: Rolled in Honduras, the Vintage 1990 wraps Dominican and Nicaraguan filler and a Nicaraguan binder in a dark Honduran broadleaf leaf aged around twelve years. The long rest has softened the leaf into a rounded, medium smoke of earth and toasted espresso with a faint vanilla sweetness, and cocoa and peppercorn gather toward the end.

thirds.notes: A mellow, loamy start with a vanilla-like undertone and toasted espresso on the finish.
Spice builds as the stronger leaf comes through, while the smoke stays smooth and round.
Baking cocoa deepens over leathery earth, with a last trace of vanilla and toasty pepper.

rocky-patel--vintage-1992.description: The Vintage 1992 pairs Dominican and Nicaraguan long filler and a Nicaraguan binder with an Ecuadorian Sumatra-seed wrapper aged about ten years. It smokes smooth and medium in body, with earth and leather under a steady line of pepper, and black coffee and a caramel-like sweetness building through the second half.

thirds.notes: An early pepper burst settles into earth and leather, with black coffee arriving late in the third.
Pepper leads over deep earth, leather and wood, with a sweet tobacco aroma.
The same core holds, joined by richer coffee and a caramel-like sweetness that lasts to the nub.

sources.title: JR Cigars Blending Room – Vintage 1992 review

rocky-patel--vintage-1999-connecticut.description: The mildest of the Vintage series is dressed in a long-aged, light tan Connecticut shade wrapper that Rocky Patel calls the oldest of its kind on the market. Smooth and creamy, it rests on a musty earth and tobacco core with a long, oily finish, picking up a syrupy sweetness and a little more body toward the end.

thirds.notes: Deep, slightly musty earth and tobacco over a creamy texture, with a long and oily finish.
Little changes: the creamy, earthy profile holds steady and stays smooth.
A syrupy sweetness joins the earth and wood, and the body grows slightly fuller.

sources.title: Cigar Obsession – Vintage Connecticut 1999 Churchill review

rocky-patel--vintage-2003-cameroon.description: An aged Cameroon wrapper covers a Nicaraguan binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler in this Vintage series blend, also offered box-pressed. Mild to medium in strength, it is sweet and aromatic: citrus and a crème brûlée-like cream at first, then vanilla, cinnamon and orange, before coffee and cedar close it out.

thirds.notes: Bright citrus fades into a sweet, custard-like creaminess.
Vanilla and cinnamon carry the middle, ending on a liqueur-like orange note.
The orange recedes for coffee and cedar, with a caramel-like sweetness on the finish.

sources.title: The Cigar Authority – Vintage 2003 Cameroon Box Press review

rocky-patel--vintage-2006-san-andres.description: Made at Rocky Patel's Nicaraguan factory in Estelí, the Vintage 2006 wraps Nicaraguan filler and a Connecticut broadleaf binder in an eleven-year-old Mexican San Andrés leaf. Dark chocolate leads from start to finish, with creamy oak, leather and black pepper, and a raisin-like sweetness that grows as the strength climbs gently toward medium.

thirds.notes: Bitter dark chocolate dominates, with creamy oak, leather, earth, hay and a raisin sweetness over black pepper.
Chocolate stays in front; espresso, anise and a light floral touch join, with pepper on the finish.
Raisin sweetness takes the lead over chocolate, espresso and salted peanuts, while the pepper fades.

sources.title: halfwheel – Vintage 2006 San Andreas Robusto review

rocky-patel--decade.description: Launched in 2007 to mark Rocky Patel's first ten years, the Decade is rolled at El Paraíso in Honduras with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It is a medium-full smoke of earth, cocoa and cedar, layered with cinnamon-like spice and pepper, and turns darker and toastier near the end.

thirds.notes: Dark tobacco, earth and a soft cocoa note, with cinnamon-like spice and pepper on the finish.
Cedar comes forward over the earth and cocoa, and a grainy sweetness appears on the finish.
Spice sharpens and darker cocoa, toasted cedar and pepper take over toward the band.

rocky-patel--the-edge-maduro.description: Part of Rocky Patel's Edge series, this Honduran-rolled cigar puts a dark maduro wrapper over a Honduran binder and Nicaraguan and Honduran filler. It is full-bodied and spicy, with black pepper and a hint of nutmeg leading into cocoa, espresso and leather, and a darker, earthier finish where the pepper returns.

thirds.notes: Black pepper and nutmeg on the retrohale, with cocoa sweetness right behind.
Espresso, dark chocolate and leather come forward, with baking spice in between.
Pepper intensifies as espresso, cocoa and earth darken and the sweetness fades.

sources.title: After Action Cigars – Edge Maduro Torpedo review

rocky-patel--the-edge-connecticut.description: The Edge Connecticut is the gentlest member of Rocky Patel's Edge series, a Honduran-collection cigar finished in a pale Connecticut wrapper. The maker describes it as mild to medium in body, a calmer way into a line otherwise known for power, offered in sizes up to the large Battalion and Howitzer.

rocky-patel--the-edge-corojo.description: The original Edge from 2004 is a Honduran-made cigar with a Corojo wrapper, a Nicaraguan binder and filler from Nicaragua, Honduras and an undisclosed third country. Despite its reputation for strength it smokes full-bodied rather than harsh: pepper and spice up front, then a woody core with almond, leather and black coffee.

thirds.notes: Spice and pepper lead, with almond and growing cedar behind a slightly sweet finish.
The pepper settles and a woody core emerges with leather, black coffee and almond.
Spice and fullness return, while earthier notes and cedar take over the finish.

sources.title: The Cigar Authority – Edge Corojo Toro review

rocky-patel--the-edge-habano.description: Rolled in Nicaragua and released in 2012, the Edge Habano covers Nicaraguan binder and filler from Estelí, Condega and Jalapa with an oily Habano-seed wrapper grown in Ecuador. Gentler than its Edge siblings, it moves from milk chocolate and coffee into a creamier middle where leather, cedar and earth dominate.

thirds.notes: Leather, sweet milk chocolate, coffee and toast, with a little black pepper.
Leather becomes dominant over coffee, cedar and earth as the smoke turns creamier.
Leather, earth and cedar remain, with a touch of chocolate and a creamy texture.

sources.title: halfwheel – The Edge Habano Toro (prerelease) review

rocky-patel--the-edge-sumatra.description: Introduced in 2007 and rolled at El Paraíso in Danlí, Honduras, the Edge Sumatra wraps a Nicaraguan binder and Honduran, Nicaraguan and Peruvian filler in a silky Ecuadorian Sumatra leaf. Its profile is built on dark cherry sweetness and leather, with a sharp woody note that grows to dominate the finish.

thirds.notes: Dark cherry sweetness and leather, with wood gaining ground as it burns.
The woody note sharpens; the cherry lightens and leather moves to the finish.
Wood dominates, leather partly returns and the fruit turns faint and tart.

sources.title: Stogie Review – Edge Sumatra Toro (2010 release) review

rocky-patel--the-edge-candela.description: The Edge Candela gives Rocky Patel's Edge series a green twist: a Habano candela wrapper, cured quickly to keep its chlorophyll colour, over an undisclosed blend. Made in a single 6 x 52 toro, it stands apart in colour and character from the darker Edge versions.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Rocky Patel Edge Candela review

thirds.notes: Wood, hay and grass at the start, quickly joined by cream and a tea-like note, with pepper far back.
Wood and tea lead as the cream fades into the background.
Pepper rises to join tea and wood and turns a little sharp near the end.

rocky-patel--the-edge-a-10.description: Created to mark ten years of the Edge series, the A-10 combines Corojo and maduro wrappers wound together in a barber-pole pattern, so each puff draws on both leaves. Rocky Patel does not publish the rest of the blend; it comes in Robusto, Toro and Sixty sizes.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Rocky Patel Edge A-10 review

thirds.notes: Espresso from the maduro and cedar from the Corojo take turns, with hay close behind and white pepper further off.
Espresso settles in front, cedar a close second and hay unchanged.
The same profile, with a little more white pepper towards the finish.

rocky-patel--the-edge-20th-anniversary.description: Released in 2022 to honour twenty years of the Edge series, this blend uses an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over Nicaraguan and Honduran binder and filler, with tobacco aged around ten years. It is medium-full in body, opening with milk chocolate, caramel, wood and nuts before turning drier, woodier and more mineral.

thirds.notes: Milk chocolate, caramel and wood, with earth and nuts up front and pepper on the retrohale.
Chocolate returns with a salty edge and steady wood, plus a lemon-tea note through the nose.
Herbal, charred wood and minerals take over as the chocolate fades, with red pepper and light cream.

sources.title: halfwheel – The Edge 20th Anniversary Toro review

rocky-patel--sun-grown.description: A Honduran blend dressed in a five-year-old, sun-grown Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper, Rocky Patel's Sun Grown is rated by the maker as medium-plus in body. It opens bold and spicy with a cedar edge, then calms into toasted bread, leather and a gentle sweetness finished with pepper, staying cool as it intensifies.

sources.title: Cigars International – Sun Grown staff review

rocky-patel--sun-grown-maduro.description: This box-pressed blend puts a dark Connecticut broadleaf maduro wrapper over a Nicaraguan binder and filler. Full in body, it moves from leather and an early burst of pepper into deepening chocolate, a creamy caramel-like sweetness and touches of wood, before coffee takes over and a nutty note closes it.

thirds.notes: An early pepper burst fades into leather, cocoa and wood, with a light cream on the finish.
Chocolate grows more intense and the finish turns creamy, with wood and a hint of espresso.
Coffee takes the lead, the chocolate sweetens and a nutty, lightly spiced finish lingers.

sources.title: He Spoke Style – Sun Grown Maduro review
The Cigar Authority – Sungrown Maduro review

rocky-patel--fifty-five.description: Fifty-Five was blended to celebrate Rocky Patel's fifty-fifth birthday: a Nicaraguan cigar with a Nicaraguan wrapper and filler held together by a Costa Rican binder. The maker places it at medium strength and body, with layered flavour and a spice that lingers on the finish.

rocky-patel--sixty.description: Blended for Rocky Patel's sixtieth birthday and rolled at his Estelí factory, the Sixty pairs a Mexican San Andrés wrapper with Nicaraguan binder and filler, and rests at least two years after rolling. Pepper and powdered cocoa open the way to deeper chocolate, round espresso and a vanilla-tinged sweetness that builds slowly.

thirds.notes: Black pepper and rich earth over powdered cocoa, with a touch of caramel sweetness.
Chocolate deepens and the espresso rounds out, with vanilla and a hint of licorice.
Pepper comes back, the cocoa turns bittersweet and the coffee roast grows heavier.

sources.title: After Action Cigars – Sixty Toro review

rocky-patel--number-6.description: Introduced in 2019, Number 6 is a Honduran puro made at Rocky Patel's El Paraíso factory under a Honduran Corojo wrapper. It is medium-bodied and approachable, a cigar for any hour: white pepper and cedar give way to cream, caramel-like sweetness, coffee and citrus.

thirds.notes: White pepper and cedar, then sweet grassy notes and a creamy, caramel-like finish.
Creamy sweetness continues with coffee and citrus, and a nutty aroma rises from the foot.
Lighter and buttery, with a salty edge and a little bitterness at the very end.

sources.title: Gotham Cigars – Rocky Patel Number 6 review

rocky-patel--sapphire.description: Made at Rocky Patel's Estelí factory, Sapphire wraps Nicaraguan and Honduran tobaccos, some from the 2014 harvest, in a Mexican San Andrés leaf. It sits at medium strength: the maker points to coffee, caramel, sweet spice and chocolate, while tasters find a creamy, earthy core with black pepper that turns mineral late on.

thirds.notes: Creaminess leads over earth, with black pepper growing on the retrohale.
A more focused black pepper sharpens the profile as the earth turns drier, then fuller.
The earth takes on a mineral, chalky tone and the pepper turns charred, over a creamy base.

rocky-patel--emerald.description: Emerald was Rocky Patel's first box-pressed cigar on the lighter side of medium: an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Nicaraguan and Mexican binders and mainly Nicaraguan filler with one Honduran Jamastrán leaf. Pepper and espresso open the way to raisin and cream, then gingerbread spice, cocoa and vanilla.

thirds.notes: A strong pepper opening with dark espresso, hay and campfire wood over raisin and sweet cream.
The pepper recedes; coffee leads with deepening gingerbread spice, smoky wood and light citrus.
Gingerbread and cinnamon take over, supported by chocolate, a crème brûlée sweetness and a floral hint.

sources.title: The Cigar Authority – Emerald Toro review

rocky-patel--grand-reserve.description: Grand Reserve is a Honduran-rolled Rocky Patel blend created for the global market, with a recipe the company keeps secret: neither wrapper, binder nor filler is disclosed. The maker describes it as medium-bodied, and it is offered in Robusto, Toro and Sixty sizes.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Rocky Patel Grand Reserve Toro review

thirds.notes: Natural tobacco leads, with dusty earth, cedar and mixed pepper behind and red pepper on the retrohale.
Earth and pepper rise, earth faster, until earth becomes the leading note.
Earth stays in front with pepper, tobacco and cedar in support to the finish.

rocky-patel--dbs-dark-broadleaf-selectio.description: DBS, short for Dark Broadleaf Selection, is built around broadleaf tobacco: a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over a binder of Nicaraguan and Pennsylvania broadleaf, with Honduran and Nicaraguan broadleaf in the filler. It is a dark, rich-looking blend offered in Robusto, Toro and Sixty formats.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Rocky Patel DBS Toro review

thirds.notes: Earth and mineral lead, mocha growing through the third, with wood and white pepper behind.
The mocha fades before the midpoint; white pepper grows on the palate and the body fills out.
White pepper joins earth and mineral in front, with mocha and wood in the background.

rocky-patel--disciple.description: Disciple is a Nicaraguan blend rolled at Rocky Patel's TAVICUSA factory in Estelí, with a dark Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. Medium to full, it opens with hay, leather and black pepper, peaks in strength with earth, roasted coffee and a hint of cocoa, and ends earthy and peppery.

thirds.notes: Hay and leather with black pepper and an earthy, meaty aftertaste.
Earth, roasted coffee beans and leather, with a hint of cocoa; the strongest stretch.
Earth and leather return with black pepper, chili heat and herbal notes.

rocky-patel--fifteenth-anniversary.description: Blended to mark Rocky Patel's fifteenth year in the cigar business, the Fifteenth Anniversary is a box-pressed cigar made from aged Nicaraguan tobaccos. The company does not break down the wrapper, binder or filler; it comes in six sizes, from a Corona Gorda to a 60-ring Sixty and a Toro in a tube.

rocky-patel--alr-second-edition.description: A.L.R. Second Edition was blended by Rocky Patel in 2016 and made in Nicaragua in a short run of around 120,000 cigars, then rested for two years in an aging room. Only the San Andrés wrapper is disclosed; the rest of the recipe stays a mystery. The maker lists it as medium to full.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Rocky Patel ALR Second Edition CDM Exclusive Robusto Grande review

thirds.notes: Earth and cocoa come forward over fruit, cedar, mineral and white pepper.
Cedar and pepper gain intensity while the cocoa recedes.
Earth stays in front with more pepper and cedar to the end.

rocky-patel--fifty.description: Fifty is a limited Rocky Patel release in a single toro, wrapped in a smooth Habano-seed oscuro leaf grown in Ecuador, over tobaccos aged upwards of eight years. The maker describes it as a complex, medium to full-bodied blend; the remaining components are not disclosed.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Rocky Patel Fifty Toro (2017) review
Cigar Coop – Rocky Patel Fifty review (2011)

thirds.notes: Cocoa and earth lead, with orange citrus, pepper, nuts and a caramel-like sweetness.
A plainer style: cedar, cherry and pepper grow, while leather appears and the sweetness fades.
Pepper and baking spice come forward with cedar and wood, and the strength builds.

rocky-patel--lb1.description: Rolled in Honduras, LB1 pairs an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper with ligero from Honduras' Jamastrán Valley and filler from Condega and Estelí in Nicaragua, all grown on Rocky Patel's own farms. The maker calls it medium-bodied; besides the usual sizes there is a Churchill with a shaggy, untrimmed foot.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Rocky Patel LB1 Robusto review

thirds.notes: Chocolate and malt open briefly before earth takes over, with citrus, cedar, a floral touch and red pepper on the retrohale.
Earth stays in front as cedar grows, citrus recedes and red pepper builds late.
Little change: earth with cedar as the main support and traces of citrus, pepper and flowers.

rocky-patel--edicion-unica.description: Edición Única began as Rocky Patel's entry for the 2011 Humo Jaguar cigar festival. It is a Honduran puro rolled at El Paraíso from tobaccos grown on small, low-yield farms, made in a single 6 x 52 toro and described by the maker as medium-bodied.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Rocky Patel Edicion Unica review

thirds.notes: Rich chocolate with light pepper, soon joined by cream and an orange citrus note.
The chocolate shifts to a classic tea flavour, the citrus fades and the pepper builds.
The pepper turns into a more exotic spice as the ligero makes itself felt, without harshness.

rocky-patel--bold-by-nish-patel.description: Bold is Nish Patel's own blend for Rocky Patel Premium Cigars: a Connecticut broadleaf maduro wrapper over tobaccos from San Andrés and the company's farms in Nicaragua. As the name suggests, it is full-bodied, rich and dense, offered in Robusto, Toro, Torpedo and Sixty sizes.

sources.title: Rocky Patel – Bold by Nish Patel
Cigar Coop – Bold by Nish Patel review

thirds.notes: Pepper first, then espresso comes forward as the pepper eases into white pepper; black cherry arrives late.
The espresso turns into dark chocolate, with cherry and pepper in the background.
White pepper takes centre stage over the dark chocolate, slightly sharp near the end.

rocky-patel--cigar-smoking-world-champio.description: Rocky Patel created this blend for the Cigar Smoking World Championship, the contest in which smokers compete to keep one cigar burning as long as possible, around the 2020 edition. It is made in a single toro; the maker does not publish its wrapper, binder or filler.

sources.title: Rocky Patel – Cigar Smoking World Championship
Cigar Coop – Rocky Patel Cigar Smoking World Championship Mareva review

thirds.notes: Distinct cocoa and espresso lead, with cedar, earth, a little fruit and red pepper on the retrohale.
Espresso takes the lead with red pepper and cedar close behind; cocoa and earth recede.
Espresso remains in front as cedar and pepper rise slightly, with fruit, earth and cocoa further back.

rocky-patel--thirtieth-anniversary.description: Marking three decades of the company, the Thirtieth Anniversary is a box-pressed Nicaraguan cigar with a San Andrés wrapper, a double Nicaraguan binder aged over seven years and Honduran and Nicaraguan filler aged five years or more. Medium to full, it carries caramel, almond and cocoa powder with a subtle cedar note.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Rocky Patel Thirtieth Toro review

thirds.notes: Mocha is prominent from the start, with earth, black pepper and a hint of mixed fruit behind.
Black coffee grows within the mocha; a brief caramel note appears before the sweetness fades.
Black coffee leads with black pepper, turning drier and more bitter towards the end.

rocky-patel--conviction.description: Conviction is a limited Nicaraguan release that draws on some of Rocky Patel's oldest stock, filler from the 2014 crop, under an oily San Andrés wrapper fermented in the Cuban terciario style. Rated medium-plus by the maker, it offers caramel and honey sweetness with coffee, espresso, chocolate and a lingering spice.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Conviction by Rocky Patel Toro review

thirds.notes: Mocha of espresso and chocolate comes forward early, with earth, red pepper, cedar and baking spice behind.
The mocha stays balanced in front as pepper, cedar and baking spice slowly build.
Pepper, cedar and baking spice reach the front beside the mocha, with earth underneath.

rocky-patel--dark-star.description: Dark Star is a Honduran cigar under a Honduran Corojo wrapper, with filler from Honduras and Paraguay alongside Nicaraguan leaf. Medium in strength and body, it is described by the maker as spicy and sweet, with dark chocolate, espresso and dried fruit.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Rocky Patel Dark Star Robusto review

thirds.notes: Coffee bean leads, with fruit, wood, mixed pepper and a musty note that slowly moves forward.
The musty note leads, then wood takes over at the midpoint as pepper increases.
Pepper and wood dominate with a musty edge; coffee and fruit are almost gone and some harshness shows.

rocky-patel--gold-label.description: Gold Label is a Nicaraguan blend with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper, a double binder of Connecticut shade and Connecticut broadleaf, and aged filler from Jalapa and Estelí. The maker lists it as medium to full, with an earthy profile of caramel and coffee and a sweetness that lingers.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Rocky Patel Gold Label Toro review

thirds.notes: Earth, cedar, raisin, mineral and cocoa, with cocoa and raisin moving forward and white pepper on the retrohale.
Raisin becomes the single lead note as pepper builds and cocoa drops back.
The raisin turns sour and pepper is the main support, with the other notes harder to pick out.

rocky-patel--white-label.description: White Label is made at Rocky Patel's own factory in Estelí: a U.S. Connecticut shade wrapper over a Nicaraguan binder, with Nicaraguan, Honduran and undisclosed filler, first shown at the 2021 PCA trade show. Medium in strength and body, it moves from cream and soft wood towards dry cedar, a trace of citrus and a slowly building pepper; a cigar for late morning.

thirds.notes: Cream, wood and cedar with a touch of citrus, the cream moving forward and black pepper on the retrohale.
Cedar strengthens and takes the lead; black pepper becomes noticeable on the palate.
Cedar stays in charge, with more pepper and wood, citrus and some cream behind it.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Rocky Patel White Label Robusto review

rocky-patel--special-edition.description: Special Edition is rolled at TAVICUSA, Rocky Patel's boutique factory in Estelí, from small-batch tobacco: an eight-year-old Ecuadorian Habano wrapper, an undisclosed double binder and Nicaraguan filler from the family's own farms. Introduced in 2016, it opens on earth, cedar and blackberry, passes through mushroom and chocolate, and ends on cedar and white pepper; an evening cigar.

thirds.notes: Earth, cedar and blackberry, then earth leads with mushroom and chocolate; white pepper and cedar on the retrohale.
Cedar grows to join earth and mushroom in front, the chocolate fading and blackberry only faint.
Cedar dominates and white pepper moves forward, with a little earth left beneath.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Rocky Patel Special Edition Toro review

rocky-patel--tavicusa.description: Named after Rocky Patel's own factory in Estelí, opened in 2008, Tavicusa was released for the factory's anniversary and shown at the 2018 IPCPR trade show. A Mexican San Andrés wrapper covers Nicaraguan binder and filler, with tobacco from Condega, Jalapa and Estelí. Medium in strength but full in body, it keeps a mocha core framed by black cherry, cedar and pepper.

thirds.notes: Mocha comes forward quickly with black cherry close behind; pepper and cedar sit further back, cedar clear on the retrohale.
Mocha stays in front and earth joins it; the cherry fades, pepper grows and the body turns full.
Mocha still leads with pepper close behind, and faint cedar and cherry linger.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Rocky Patel TAVICUSA Robusto review
